properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 19 at 1:29PM MDT until September 19 at 4:30PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
FFWGJT

The National Weather Service in Grand Junction has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Lee burn scar in...
Northeastern Rio Blanco County in northwestern Colorado...

* Until 430 PM MDT.

* At 129 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain over the Lee Burn Scar. Between 0.25 and 0.75 inches of
rain have fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 1 to 3 inches in 1
hour. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.25 to 0.5 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly. Excessive rainfall over the warning area will
cause mud slides near steep terrain. The mud slide can consist of
rock, mud, vegetation and other loose materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Lee Burn Scar.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Lee Burn Scar.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of Northeastern Rio Blanco County.
properties.instruction:
This is a life threatening situation. Heavy rainfall will cause
extensive and severe flash flooding of creeks...streams...and ditches
in the Lee Burn Scar. Severe debris flows can also be anticipated
across roads. Roads and driveways may be washed away in places. If
you encounter flood waters...climb to safety.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued September 19 at 1:51PM MDT until September 19 at 2:30PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
SVRABQ

The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Northwestern Valencia County in central New Mexico...
East Central Cibola County in west central New Mexico...

* Until 230 PM MDT.

* At 151 PM MDT, a severe thunderstorm was located near New Laguna,
or near Laguna Pueblo, moving east at 15 mph.

HAZARD...Ping pong ball size hail and 60 mph wind gusts.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...People and animals outdoors will be injured. Expect hail
damage to roofs, siding, windows, and vehicles. Expect
wind damage to roofs, siding, and trees.

* Locations impacted include...
Laguna Pueblo, Mesita, New Laguna and Paraje.

This includes Interstate 40 between Mile Markers 108 and 126.
properties.instruction:
Seek shelter inside a well-built structure and stay away from
windows. This storm is capable of producing damaging winds and large
hail.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 19 at 1:01PM MDT until September 19 at 4:00PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
FFWABQ

The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northeastern Cibola County in west central New Mexico...

* Until 400 PM MDT.

* At 101 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.25 to 0.75 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
McCartys, Skyline-Ganipa, San Fidel, Cubero, Acomita Lake, Acomita,
North Acomita Village, Seama and Paraje.

This includes Interstate 40 between Mile Markers 87 and 107.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.
